parole.testo: Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *yugóm. Compare Old Polish igo.

parole.significato: synonym of kąsać (“to bite, to sting”)
parole.testo: Derived from Proto-Indo-European *Hrewp- (“to break, to tear up”). Compare Latvian rūpēt, Lithuanian rūpėti and Russian ру́пить (rúpitʹ).

Inherited from Old Polish rydz. By surface analysis, back-formation from rydzy. Cognate with Bulgarian рижика (rižika), Russian ры́жик (rýžik). Compare Spanish robellón (distantly cognate via Proto-Indo-European *h₁rewdʰ-).

From German Ferkel + -ę. Per Brückner, a native word, derived from Proto-Indo-European *wérsēn (“virile man, male animal”). Akin to Latin verrēs (“boar”), Latvian vērsis (“ox”), Lithuanian ver̃šis (“calf, ox”), Old Prussian werstian (“calf”), Sanskrit वृषन् (vṛ́ṣan, “male, bull, stallion”).
